guard: the manager's cooperative stop joins queued event work before it exits
why: The join is what makes NOTHING MAY PUBLISH AFTER TEARDOWN true on the path a supervised seat
actually takes. It went into the plugin-unload path first, with that sentence above it, while the
manager's stop ran a separate routine that exited without joining, so the claim was false exactly
where it mattered. Both ways out now call one bounded teardown.
THE TWO JOINS COVER DIFFERENT CASES AND ARE GRADED SEPARATELY. The holder join covers event work
already running; the chain join covers a swap queued but not yet begun. C1 removes both and grades
that the teardown joins anything at all. C3 removes only the chain join, which the running case
cannot detect because the holder join catches it, and is reddened by the queued case instead.
C4 GRADES THE ORDER, NOT SUFFICIENCY AGAINST THE REAL KILL, and that boundary is measured rather
than assumed. A leg that stopped a seat and killed it after a short grace was built twice and
discarded twice, because it passed on BOTH arms: losing the connection purges the presence entry,
so a roster read after a kill says offline whether or not the seat published it, and a read taken
before the kill did not redden either. Cells that cannot fail are worse than absent ones, so it is
not here. What remains graded is that presence does not queue behind the drain.
C6 GRADES THE FENCE, C7 AND C8 GRADE THE WIRING, and they are different claims. C6 asks whether
the refusal refuses; C7 and C8 ask whether a given door actually goes THROUGH it, which is the
failure a shared guard is meant to prevent and which no amount of grading the guard itself can
see. Both are needed because a helper nothing routes to is a helper that guards nothing.
chat.message IS FENCED BUT NOT GRADED, stated rather than left to be discovered. Its only
post-teardown effect is a card-model publish, and that publish carries the STORED status, which
is already offline, so there is no presence-visible harm to key a cell on. The probe knocks on it
so the door is exercised, but mutating it out of the table would survive, and no claim here
covers it.
C9 IS A FOURTH DOOR AND NOT A FOURTH COPY OF THE SAME ONE. The tool map never passes through
the hook table: OpenCode is handed those closures at registration, so fencing the table left
them open. It is graded through cotal_status because that is the cotal_* tool with a
presence-visible effect; the others are fenced by the same wrapper but their harm is a channel
write, which this harness does not watch.

mutations.name: C1 the shared teardown stops joining the event work at all, so a stop abandons a drain that was already in flight
mutations.find:
await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
    await settleWithin(events?.settled(), SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "event holder at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: cooperative stop joined the queued event work before exiting

mutations.name: C2 a turn may start mid-cutover again, so an ordinary inbound message prompts the new session before its replacement holder is installed
mutations.expectRed: no turn was started while the cutover was open

mutations.name: C3 the teardown joins only the holder, so a swap that was still QUEUED when the stop arrived is abandoned unrun
mutations.find: await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
mutations.expectRed: a swap still QUEUED at the stop was allowed to run before exit

mutations.name: C4 leaving the mesh queues behind the drain again, so a seat whose drain outlives the runtime's grace window is killed before its presence goes offline
mutations.find:
await safeStatus("offline");
    await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
mutations.replace:
await settleWithin(swapChain, SWAP_SETTLE_MS, "swap chain at teardown");
    await safeStatus("offline");
mutations.expectRed: the seat left the mesh BEFORE the drain finished, not behind it

mutations.name: C5 teardown stops being a refusal, so the swap's deferred drive starts a NEW turn while the stop is still joining the chain, after presence has gone offline
mutations.expectRed: the teardown started no turn of its own after the stop began

mutations.name: C6 the fence stops refusing, so every public hook entry keeps admitting work after teardown began and a late presence publish puts the seat back on the mesh it just left
mutations.find: async (...args: never[]): Promise<unknown> => (stopping ? undefined : await hook(...args)),
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh

mutations.name: C7 the tool hook is wired past the fence instead of through it, which is exactly the omission a single shared guard is supposed to make impossible
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh

mutations.name: C8 the event hook is wired past the fence instead of through it, so a late permission.asked republishes presence over the offline record
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh

mutations.name: C9 the tool map stops refusing, so a cotal_* call still inside the model's turn runs after the stop and its presence write puts the seat back on the mesh
mutations.find: stopping ? `⚠ ${name} was not run: this seat is shutting down` : await def.execute(...args),
mutations.expectRed: nothing admitted after teardown began put the seat back on the mesh
